analysis: This PR adds only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/reasoning-stop-outside-reasoning.md, lines 1-18) and an update to the `stop` row in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 2126) plus the date at line 3. No executable code is in the supplied batch, so nothing here changes authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, billing or data exposure. The documented behavior is that client stop sequences on Gemma 4 and `<think>` models match only returned `content`, with reasoning spans and tool-call spans excluded by `ReasoningStopScope`. Stops still apply to literal tool tags when the request has no tool handler. This is a functional and availability correctness change in the TB-007 inference path. It does not touch the coordinator-to-provider encryption boundary (TB-002, T-008) or the prefix cache (T-041). I found no security regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption in the docs. Open questions for integration, which the supplied evidence cannot settle: the actual implementation (`ReasoningStopScope`, `StopHoldback`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) is not in this batch. Whether the described scope can leak reasoning text into `content` via stop-sequence replay, or can stop suppression by a crafted frame (e.g. arguments quoting a closing tag) cause unbounded generation (T-010, T-029), should be checked against the code PR if it is reviewed separately. The doc claims only that such frames are an exception, so this is not a documentation defect.
